hints: Notice the newton meter falls from $W$ in air to $P$ in water and to $Q$ in oil, so $W-P$ and $W-Q$ are the two upthrust forces.
Recall upthrust equals weight of displaced fluid, $U = \rho V g$, with the same object volume $V$ completely immersed in each liquid.
Divide the oil upthrust expression by the water upthrust expression so $V$ and $g$ cancel and leave $\rho_{oil}/\rho_{water}$ in terms of $W$, $P$ and $Q$.
walkthrough: Identify the forces: in air tension $= W$, in liquid tension $+$ upthrust $= W$, so upthrust $=$ loss of apparent weight.
In water, upthrust is $U_{water} = W - P$. In oil, upthrust is $U_{oil} = W - Q$.
Use Archimedes principle: $U = \rho_{fluid} V g$, where $V$ is the volume of the object, the same in both cases because it is completely immersed.
Write $U_{oil} = \rho_{oil} V g$ and $U_{water} = \rho_{water} V g$.
Divide to eliminate the common $V g$: $\frac{\rho_{oil}}{\rho_{water}} = \frac{U_{oil}}{U_{water}}$.
Substitute the upthrusts: $\frac{\rho_{oil}}{\rho_{water}} = \frac{W-Q}{W-P}$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This inverts the fluids and uses $Q-P$ which is the difference between the two apparent weights, not the upthrust in either fluid.

B.explanation: The numerator $Q-P$ is the difference in upthrusts, not the upthrust in oil, so it cannot give $\rho_{oil}$ alone.

C.explanation: This is the inverse ratio $\rho_{water}/\rho_{oil}$ because $W-P$ is the larger water upthrust and $W-Q$ is the oil upthrust.

D.explanation: The upthrusts $W-Q$ in oil and $W-P$ in water are proportional to $\rho_{oil}$ and $\rho_{water}$, so their ratio gives the density ratio.
